question: Which occupation consistently borrowed the largest sums, with data to back up this assertion?
title: Occupations owing the largest sums
understood: 'Borrowed' = owed the estate in a de dare entry; occupation = an occupation tag linked to the debtor. Size is the median debt, florins and lire ranked separately; 'consistently' = whether the ranking holds year by year.
limits: Only 10 of 38 included pages are tagged and none of the sums has been checked; few debts carry a date, so year-by-year consistency cannot really be tested yet.

answer.headline: Not yet answerable with confidence: the largest single debt is a vinattiere's (ƒ 176 plus ℔ 79), but every occupation rests on one to three machine-read sums, so no occupation is shown to borrow large sums consistently.
answer.answer:
Read as 'owed the estate in a de dare entry', the 10 tagged pages of MPAP 4 give 63 debts with a tagged debtor [debts]. Only 26 of them name the debtor's occupation, 47 have a sum, none of those sums has been checked yet, and 17 carry a rule warning.

In florins, the vinattiere ranks first by both median and total: Bartolo di Nese, vinattiere “da cā mignano”, owes ƒ 176 ℔ 79 ß 16 𝒹 2 on RS1123 [occ_fl] [occ_fl_total]. That is one entry. The next occupations (albergatore ƒ 14.34, lavoratore ƒ 6, speziale ƒ 4) also rest on a single florin sum each. In lire the order is vinattiere (℔ 79.81), lavoratore (℔ 64.88, Domenicuccio d'Andrea), tessitore di drappi (℔ 23.23), then sarto, speziale and maestro, all under ℔ 7 [occ_li]. Only maestro (3 sums, median ℔ 4.35) and biadaiolo (2 sums) have more than one lire sum.

Consistency cannot be tested. Only 8 of the 63 debts carry a date (1388 and 1389), and each occupation appears in at most one dated year [occ_fl] [occ_li]. When sums the rules flagged are left out, the vinattiere's debt drops out (its sum has a plain 'd' read as denari) and the albergatore leads in florins with ƒ 14.34 [occ_fl_clean]. So the ranking depends on a single unchecked line.

What the data does show: a vinattiere and a lavoratore owed the two largest debts in this sample, in both currencies, far above the typical debt (median ƒ 3.5 and ℔ 2 among debtors with no recorded occupation).

claims.text: The largest single debt with a recorded occupation is the vinattiere Bartolo di Nese's: ƒ 176 ℔ 79 ß 16 𝒹 2 pc̄.
Each occupation's ranking rests on 1–3 sums; no occupation has more than 3 sums in either currency.
Whether any occupation 'consistently' owed more cannot be tested: 8 of 63 debts are dated, in two years.
Leaving out flagged sums changes the florin leader from vinattiere to albergatore.

caveats: Many of these debts are arrears carried over from Deo's books ('levammo dal memoriale', 'a libro giallo'): they are what people owed the estate, often rents or purchases, not necessarily loans.
followups: Check the 47 sums behind the debts in the Sums tab (start with RS1123 line of Bartolo di Nese and RS1126 Domenicuccio d'Andrea).
